nominations.title: [ABSTRACT] "Adding one trace term per candidate removes the bias and restores complete-data-equivalent selection."
nominations.reason: The body shows only that the bias is removed in expectation and that selection is 'substantially' restored with a residual gap/floor; 'restores complete-data-equivalent selection' is stronger than the demonstrated rate-level recovery.

nominations.title: [S1-P4] "In our pre-registered study, every misclassification by uncorrected MI-AIC chose the candidate with the largest RIV."
nominations.reason: Body limits this to congenial cells ('In every congenial cell, all of the uncorrected criterion's errors land on the saturated... candidate'); the unqualified 'every misclassification' overstates what S5-P17 shows.

nominations.title: [S1-P4] "We show that the corrected criterion recovers its complete-data expectation at any signal strength."
nominations.reason: The criterion-level expectation recovery is shown, but 'at any signal strength' is asserted broadly while the weak-signal cell exhibits a floor; the phrase blurs second-level (criterion) and third-level (rate) results.

nominations.title: [S1-P5] "Correction then restores complete-data behavior entirely."
nominations.reason: The ladder results show two-moment/equating arms reach the benchmark only in the strong-signal cell and not in the weak-signal cell, so 'entirely' overstates the demonstrated case.

nominations.title: [S1-P5] "we show that no transformation of the observed data can recover it"
nominations.reason: G4 explicitly concedes 'No argument here shows that no estimator built from the same observed data could do better,' contradicting the impossibility claim stated in the intro.

nominations.title: [S1-P3] "The principle as an explicit yardstick is, to our knowledge, stated here for the first time."
nominations.reason: A novelty/priority claim ('to our knowledge... first time') that the prose cannot itself substantiate beyond hedging; a careful reviewer flags such first-claims as unverifiable as written.

nominations.title: [S1-P1] "On that testimony, the major inferential questions read as settled."
nominations.reason: Sweeping characterization of the field's state attributed to cited reviews but stated more broadly than those accounts ('point estimates recover... Wald-type tests... well calibrated') can carry without qualification.

nominations.title: [S1B-P1] "a kind of collaboration that is new in the age of AI and whose products are not yet routinely trusted"
nominations.reason: Empirical sociological assertion about trust and novelty offered without citation or evidence.

nominations.title: [S1B-P1] "Productive means that the collaboration reached results a single author would have reached slowly or not at all."
nominations.reason: Counterfactual productivity claim with no controlled comparison; the coded transcript counts measure activity, not that a solo author could not have reached the results.

nominations.title: [S1B-P2] "This section describes the collaboration and shows that it was active and human-directed."
nominations.reason: The counts show interventions occurred but 'human-directed' as a conclusion is asserted beyond what turn-tallies establish, especially since the coding was done by the same kind of system.

nominations.title: [S1-P6b] "removes the bias and substantially restores the ranking that complete data would have given"
nominations.reason: Acceptable as 'substantially' here, but pairs with the abstract's stronger 'restores complete-data-equivalent selection'; flagged for internal inconsistency in strength of claim across the paper.

nominations.title: [S5-P14] "The size-adjusted power arms are the partial support cited for the power conjecture of @sec-discussion."
nominations.reason: The figure and text say raw power is not compared and is confounded; the 'size-adjusted power arms' providing support are asserted but no size-adjusted comparison is actually reported in the results.

nominations.title: [S5-P15] "Both match the projected-trace prediction of $2.64$. Correctness rests on that match."
nominations.reason: 'Correctness rests on that match' overstates a single engineered-cell discrimination result as establishing the formula's correctness generally.

nominations.title: [S5-P22] "This robustness is empirical and scoped to the designs studied."
nominations.reason: The opening sentence 'bounds the cost of not running data augmentation' claims a bound, but only a 2–3% agreement on studied cells is shown, not a derived bound—internally hedged but headline overclaims.

nominations.title: [S3-P6] "A derivation produced and checked within a single model family would likely have shipped one sign without noticing that there was a choice."
nominations.reason: Counterfactual about single-family workflows asserted without evidence; the observed 8-of-9 figure is cross-family, not a controlled single-family comparison.

nominations.title: [S6-P5] "We conjecture that the bias-corrected likelihood-ratio comparison dominates its uncorrected counterpart in power uniformly."
nominations.reason: Labeled a conjecture but 'uniformly' is a strong universal claim whose 'partial support' is the confounded power arms the simulation section says cannot be compared.

nominations.title: [S6-P7] "No transformation of the observed data manufactures the lost evidence back."
nominations.reason: Restates the impossibility claim that G4 explicitly disclaims ('No argument here shows that no estimator... could do better'), creating a direct internal contradiction.

nominations.title: [S6-P7b] "Then trust the result the way complete-data results are trusted."
nominations.reason: A blanket practical endorsement that ignores the paper's own scope limits (estimated-scale, congeniality, weak-signal floor, normal-only verification) stated immediately above it.

nominations.title: [S5-P18] "The junk cell closes $90$ percent of the gap from uncorrected to benchmark."
nominations.reason: The reader cannot reconstruct '90 percent' from the table without specifying which arm; the table shows uncorrected 0.422, two-moment 0.702, benchmark 0.727, which is ~92% for two-moment—the unspecified arm leaves the figure underspecified.

nominations.title: [S1-P2] "That study also cautions that selecting models by averaged criteria has no support in the multiple-imputation literature."
nominations.reason: Characterizes a cited study's caution in absolute terms ('no support'); as written the strong paraphrase risks overstating the source's hedge.

bench: [S2-P3] 'the weakest general conditions for ignoring the mechanism' — strong characterization stated without internal support
[S1B-P2] '599 substantive human turns' coded counts presented as fact while coding done by same-kind system
[S6-P8] 'Whether this workflow generalizes beyond one paper is asserted, not demonstrated' — self-aware but the surrounding workflow-promotion still leans on it
[S5-P17] 'the saturated model is the natural destination for any downward-biased deviance' — plausibility argument stated as if established
[S6-P4b] uncongenial overshoot 'marks where the framework's safety margin ends' — interpretive claim from one stress cell
gaps: missing-citation is thin: most issues are overclaim/speculation; few prose claims clearly lack a needed external reference since field-state claims do carry citekeys.
